title: Three-tier swipe: Save / Play Next / Play Now
description:
## Summary
Implement three-tier right-swipe gesture on ArticleRowView with progressive actions:

1. **Short swipe (~80pt)**: Save article (bookmark only, no queue)
2. **Medium swipe (~150pt)**: Save + Play Next (add after current item)
3. **Full swipe (~220pt)**: Save + Play Now (insert at front, start playback)

## Current State
- Single threshold at 100pt triggers save + add to end of queue
- `actionButtonsOverlay` exists but disabled (ArticleRowView.swift:434-481)
- `performSaveAction()` comment: 'Dont show action buttons'

## Files to Modify
- `Briefeed/Features/Article/ArticleRowView.swift`

## API Already Exists
```swift
// AudioPlayerViewModelV2.swift:360
func addToQueue(_ article: Article, playNow: Bool = false, playNext: Bool = false) async
```

## Required Changes
1. Replace single `swipeThreshold` (100pt) with three thresholds:
   - `saveThreshold = 80`
   - `playNextThreshold = 150` 
   - `playNowThreshold = 220`

2. Add enum for action tiers:
   ```swift
   enum SwipeActionTier { case save, playNext, playNow }
   ```

3. Update visual indicators:
   - Icon changes: bookmark -> list.number -> play.fill
   - Text changes: Save -> Play Next -> Play Now
   - Color: light green -> medium green -> bright green

4. Add distinct haptic at each threshold

5. Refactor `performSaveAction(tier: SwipeActionTier)`

6. Remove timer-based overlay (no longer needed)

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Short swipe saves article without queuing
- [ ] Medium swipe saves and inserts after current item
- [ ] Full swipe saves, inserts at front, starts playback
- [ ] Visual feedback indicates current action tier
- [ ] Haptic feedback distinguishes tiers
- [ ] Elastic resistance beyond full swipe threshold

title: Mini player title has transparent background causing text overlap
description:
## Problem
The mini player title section in MiniAudioPlayerV4.swift has a semi-transparent background (30% opacity at line 43):

```swift
.background(Color(UIColor.secondarySystemBackground).opacity(0.3))
```

This allows the FeedView article list content to bleed through, causing article titles from the scrolling list to overlap with the currently playing title.

## Evidence
Text shows garbled characters like 'When a robot cAntellsAvou to lstop...' which is actually two titles overlapping:
- 'When a robot can tell you to stop, do you listen?' (current track)
- 'Anti-Aging Injection Regimen' (article in feed list below)

## Fix
Change line 43 in MiniAudioPlayerV4.swift from:
```swift
.background(Color(UIColor.secondarySystemBackground).opacity(0.3))
```
to:
```swift
.background(Color(UIColor.secondarySystemBackground))
```

## File Location
Briefeed/Features/Audio/MiniAudioPlayerV4.swift:43
close_reason: Fixed by removing opacity(0.3) from mini player title background
